description: Opens a sqlite3.Connection with the pragmas required by ADR-001 (WAL mode, foreign keys on, synchronous=NORMAL), creating the parent directory of db_path on demand.
docstring:
Open a configured SQLite connection.

Args:
    db_path: Absolute path to the database file. Parent directories are created if missing.

Returns:
    An open sqlite3.Connection with journal_mode=WAL, foreign_keys=ON and synchronous=NORMAL applied, row_factory set to sqlite3.Row, and an internal thread-id tag recorded for later cross-thread-use detection by the other storage functions.

Raises:
    StorageError: If the underlying sqlite3.connect call fails (e.g. db_path's parent cannot be created due to a permissions error).
preconditions: db_path is an absolute pathlib.Path (callers resolve relative paths before calling, per config.Settings)
postconditions: The connection is tagged with threading.get_ident() at creation time so a later call from a different thread can be detected and rejected

edge_cases.input: db_path's parent directory does not exist
edge_cases.expected_behavior: parent directories are created (mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)) before connecting

edge_cases.input: db_path points to a location without write permission
db_path already exists as a valid, older-schema database
edge_cases.expected_behavior: connects successfully; initialize_schema/migrate are separate, explicit steps, not run implicitly by get_connection

unit_tests.name: test_pragmas_applied
unit_tests.description: A fresh connection reports WAL mode and foreign_keys=1.

unit_tests.name: test_creates_missing_parent_directory
unit_tests.description: db_path under a nonexistent directory tree still succeeds.

unit_tests.name: test_unwritable_path_raises_storage_error
unit_tests.description: A read-only target directory raises StorageError.
